scholarly_atoms.title: The International Criminal Court
scholarly_atoms.knowledge_summary: While global civil society does not deliver global democracy, it does contribute to more transparent, more deliberative and more ethical international decision-making which is ultimately preferable to a world of isolated sovereign states with no accountability outside their borders, or exclusive and secretive state-to-state diplomacy. A new examination of the International Criminal Court (ICC) from a political science and international relations perspective. It also delivers essential background to the place of the US in international relations and makes a major contribution to thinking about the ICC’s future. This book will be of great interest to students and scholars of international relations, international law, globalization and global governance. It also makes these issues accessible to non-lawyers and presents effective advocacy strategies for non-governmental organizations.

scholarly_atoms.title: International Multilateral Negotiation: Approaches to the Management of Complexity

source_identity.publisher_or_journal: IIASA PURE (International Institute of Applied Systems Analysis)

scholarly_atoms.knowledge_summary: To show how these approaches work in actual practice, the authors provide detailed analyses of two multilateral negotiations -- the Uruguay round of negotiations under the General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and the negotiations leading to the Single European Act consolidating the European Community. In a single volume, a team of distinguished international scholars draws on a wide range of social science theory to explain the dynamics of bargaining and diplomacy when many parties and many issues are involved. \n\nThe book provides the tools for analyzing and managing the complexities of multilateral negotiations including: How the roots of conflict, the distribution of power, and specific patterns of resistance and cooperation affect all stages of negotiation. How insights in to the way small groups function can help advance negotiations.
